channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ratinho fala sobre suposta amante e surpreende: "Eu tenho seis"
item.description: Ratinho criticized the 'mimimi' culture on social media, claiming false news and political polarization are disrupting Brazilians' lives. He jokingly responded to rumors of having a lover by saying he 'has six,' using irony. Silvia Abravanel, a federal deputy candidate, supported his views, noting that fake news are often created to damage public figures' reputations.

item.title: Argentino indiciado no inquérito da tentativa de golpe é detido
item.description: Argentine political strategist Fernando Cerimedo, former advisor to Javier Milei and current aide to Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz, was detained in Bolivia over suspected involvement in a shooting attack against his ex-girlfriend, lawyer Nadia Beller, in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Beller claimed Paz does not govern Bolivia and that Cerimedo does, alleging she saw 'drawers full of money' at his home. Cerimedo was previously indicted in Brazil in 2024 in the coup attempt investigation but not charged, and has participated in events with figures like Eduardo Bolsonaro to challenge the credibility of Brazil’s electoral system.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro pretende seguir cartilha de Lula em 2018
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) campaign has decided to follow the PT's 2018 playbook by exploiting the image of Jair Bolsonaro through AI-generated videos, while the TSE has not yet ruled on the legality of such content. The exclusive article highlights the intention to replicate past campaign tactics.

item.title: Ir ou não ir a debates?
item.description: A poll of 671 readers asked whether Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro should participate in the 2026 presidential debates. 37% said yes, 32.2% said no, and 30.8% believed the decision should be individual. The content does not mention specific policy proposals or stances on particular issues.

item.title: Saiba em quais países a Lava Jato não acabou
item.description: While the Lava Jato operation was largely annulled in Brazil by the STF, it remains active in at least five countries, including Peru, the United States, and the United Kingdom, where convictions, leniency agreements, and asset seizures have been upheld. In Peru, former presidents Alejandro Toledo and Ollanta Humala were convicted of receiving Odebrecht bribes, with Toledo facing over 33 years in prison across two cases. Nadine Heredia, Humala’s wife, sought diplomatic asylum in Brazil to avoid immediate imprisonment in Peru.

item.title: Eleição de 2026 tem recorde de 191 candidaturas indígenas
item.description: The 2026 elections feature a record 191 indigenous candidacies, a 125% increase from 2014. Of these, 75 are running for the Chamber of Deputies and 99 for state assemblies, with 44% women and representation from 64 indigenous peoples, concentrated in the Legal Amazon.

item.title: Candidaturas com termos religiosos na urna caem 42%
item.description: In 2026, the number of candidacies with religious terms in the ballot name fell by 42% compared to 2022, dropping from 657 to 381 records, according to a Poder360 survey using TSE data. Evangelical terms dominate, accounting for 93.2% of cases (355 records), with 'pastor' being the most common (179 candidacies). MDB leads among parties with the most candidates using religious terms (34), followed by PL (32) and Novo (31).

item.title: Bets: Lula foca saúde, Flávio veta auxílio e Caiado bane propaganda
item.description: Lula focuses on mental health and credit control to address online betting harms, expanding SUS mental health services and regulating financial institutions. Flávio Bolsonaro proposes banning the use of social program funds for gambling and promoting financial education through Caixa. Ronaldo Caiado advocates for a total ban on betting advertising, sets spending limits, and strengthens actions against illegal platforms and money laundering.

item.title: Haddad e Tarcísio travam embate de indicadores criminais
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad are focusing their campaigns for the São Paulo gubernatorial race on public security, with the incumbent governor increasing crime-related mentions in his platform from 23 to 54, proposing initiatives such as an Intelligence and Innovation Center (CIN), expansion of the SP Mobile app, and enhanced protection for women. Haddad challenges the transparency of current crime statistics and promises a new auditable methodology to evaluate the administration's performance.

item.title: União Brasil e PP lançam 1,3 mil candidatos a menos que em 2022 após federação
item.description: União Brasil and PP, united in a federation since March 2024, launched 828 and 709 candidates respectively for the 2026 elections, totaling 1,537 — 1,300 fewer than in 2022. The reduction reflects a strategy to unify bases and optimize resources following the formation of the party federation. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Canabidiol, lobby e minuta de contrato: o que revelam as mensagens de Marcola e amiga de Lulinha
item.description: WhatsApp intercepts by the Federal Police reveal that Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), former chief of staff to President Lula, received a draft contract to bypass bidding for cannabis-based products for the SUS, lobbied by Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of the president’s son, Lulinha. Luchsinger was paid R$1.5 million to lobby the Health Ministry and also covered expenses and gifts for Marcola, including R$9,200 in jewelry. Although Marcola’s defense claims the contract never proceeded and he reimbursed the amounts, investigations suggest possible influence peddling involving Lulinha and the lobbyist, with cases under review at the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Ministros do TSE indicam que devem tirar Marçal da disputa presidencial
item.description: Members of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) indicated they will likely deny the presidential candidacy registration of Pablo Marçal (PRTB) for the 2026 election due to his ineligibility, confirmed in first and second instances by the Electoral Justice. The São Paulo Regional Electoral Court (TRE-SP) had already unanimously rejected Marçal’s appeals on August 5, upholding the ineligibility ruling. This bars him from running in the 2026 presidential race unless overturned by a higher court.

item.title: Empresário de AL declara R$ 30 milhões em dinheiro vivo; veja ranking
item.description: Luiz Teodoro dos Santos, an Avante candidate for the Chamber of Deputies from Alagoas, declared R$ 30 million in cash to the TSE in the 2026 elections, leading the ranking of the highest cash declaration among candidates. The amount represents one of the highest ever recorded in asset disclosures in Brazil, raising questions about the origin and transparency of the funds.

item.title: Ex-chefe do BC e e ex-ministro de Temer estão entre os maiores doadores da campanha; veja quem são
item.description: The top 15 individual donors in Brazil's electoral campaigns so far have directed funds to state and national party directories, as well as candidates for governor and legislative seats in several states. The largest donation came from former minister Fabiano Silveira, who gave R$2 million to the MDB in Paraíba. Minas Gerais Governor Mateus Simões received the highest individual amount among candidates in this group, with R$500 thousand from Alfonso G.

item.title: Flávio usa estratégia da esperança que virou ‘morte’ e ‘dívida’ para tirar votos de Lula no Nordeste
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign aims to undermine Lula's stronghold in the Northeast by reframing the 'hope' narrative as linked to 'debt' (cost of living and Bolsa Família), 'death' (femicide), and 'shame' (rising homelessness), targeting female voters through radio and TV ads. Despite local resistance, even from PL allies, the strategy seeks to gain crucial tenths of a percentage point in a projected tight race.

item.title: VÍDEO: entenda o que são votos válidos e como eles são calculados nas pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: The video explains the concept of valid votes in electoral polls, detailing how Datafolha and Quaest calculate them differently. While Datafolha excludes blank, null, and undecided votes to align with the TSE’s method, Quaest uses a 'likely voters' model. The goal is to help the public correctly interpret polls as the 2026 elections approach.

item.title: Lobista postou foto em mansão usada para reuniões com Lulinha no dia de operação da PF sobre fraudes do INSS
item.description: Businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, identified by the Federal Police as a lobbyist, posted photos from a rented mansion in Lago Sul, Brasília, on the same day she was targeted in Operation Sem Desconto, which investigates illegal diversion of INSS pensions. The property was used for meetings with clients and frequently visited by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula, both under investigation at the STF for alleged influence trafficking. Luchsinger was subject to a search and seizure warrant in São Paulo on December 18, 2025, and posted the photos that same day, showing her presence at the residence amid the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio não vê com maus olhos entrada de Marçal na disputa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign does not view Pablo Marçal's entry into the 2026 presidential race negatively, citing common ground in their ideas. Despite Marçal's ineligibility until 2032 due to TRE-SP convictions for misuse of social media and illicit fundraising, his candidacy is seen as a potential springboard for discussing Flávio's proposals, posing no real threat.

item.title: Loterj: Empresa ligada a aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro e Castro segue na mira da Justiça
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro State Lottery (Loterj), under interim management of Ricardo Couto, is attempting to recover millions of reais owed by Rio Pag, a company linked to an ally of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Governor Cláudio Castro, related to payment processing contracts for lottery and betting services. The contract, inherited from the previous administration, has become a legal and financial burden for the agency. The exclusive article highlights potential irregularities in public-private ties involving politically connected firms.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja datas, regras, cargos em disputa e como votar
item.description: Brazil's 2026 general elections will take place in two rounds: October 4 (first round) and October 26 (second round, if needed), to elect president, governor, senator, federal and state/district deputies. Voting is mandatory for literate citizens aged 18 to 70, optional for illiterates, those over 70, and 16–17-year-olds. To run, candidates must have Brazilian nationality, party affiliation, electoral domicile in the region for at least six months, and meet the minimum age requirement for each office.

item.title: Descoberta na Foz do Amazonas só será 'passaporte para o futuro' se modelo adotado no pré-sal mudar, diz ex-diretor da Petrobras
item.description: Ildo Sauer, former Petrobras director, says the oil discovery in the Amazon Foz will only be a 'passport to the future' if the exploration model used in the pre-salt is changed. He argues that pre-salt revenues were 'wasted' and not invested in public policies like education, health, pensions, and energy transition, advocating for stronger state control via Petrobras to fund national development.

item.title: Eleições 2026: candidatos a presidente iniciam campanhas pelo Nordeste
item.description: Presidential candidates Renan Santos (Mission) and Wilson Grassi (Democrat) launched their Northeastern campaigns this Wednesday with events in Paraíba and Bahia. Lula (PT) will visit Rio Grande do Norte on Thursday to strengthen support in the region, historically favorable to him, including institutional visits and a campaign event at the Dunas Arena in Natal.

item.title: Após repercussão, entorno de Kassab se divide sobre criticas a Flavio
item.description: Following Gilberto Kassab's (PSD) statement that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has 'zero' chance of winning, the circle around PSD president and presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado is divided between those advocating stronger criticism of the senator and those warning against alienating right-wing voters. While one faction views the Centrão's neutrality as beneficial to Lula and supports Kassab's stance, another criticizes the strategy for risking Caiado's image as an opportunist. Flávio Bolsonaro and his campaign responded by accusing the PSD of acting as a 'PT auxiliary line', using Kassab's remarks to mobilize their digital base.

item.title: Com 568 nomes, PL é o partido com mais candidatos ao Senado e Câmara
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) has the highest number of candidates in the 2026 elections, with 568 registrations — 535 for federal deputy and 33 for senator — according to TSE data. This electoral offensive aims to make the PL the dominant force in Congress starting in 2027, projecting the election of 20 new senators to grow its bench to 28 members and securing the largest share of the electoral fund (Fundão) in 2026, approximately R$ 881.6 million.

item.title: Planalto e campanha de Lula silenciam sobre contrato enviado por amiga de Lulinha à ex-chefe de gabinete de presidente
item.description: Lula's campaign and the Planalto remained silent on a Federal Police investigation revealing that former chief of staff Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro received a contract for cannabidiol sales to the Health Ministry without bidding, sent by businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Lulinha, the president's son. The case is tied to STF inquiries on influence peddling, and Roberta also received R$1.5 million from 'Careca do INSS', a suspect in pension fund fraud, raising concerns about illicit influence in government contracts.

item.title: Na véspera de julgamento no STF sobre mandato tampão de governador, Couto passa o dia em Brasília em reuniões sobre dívida do estado
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Ricardo Couto, spent the day in Brasília meeting with the Ministry of Finance to discuss the restructuring of the state's R$ 26 billion debt, ahead of the STF's ruling on the interim governorship. The judgment, which will determine whether he remains in office until the October elections, hinges on six undecided justices, with the possibility of a vista request delaying the process beyond the election date. Meanwhile, Couto's administration continues with budget cuts, agency eliminations, and audits, including one that led to 35 dismissals in an elderly support program.

item.title: Lulinha e Marcola viram "trunfos" em campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign plans to use investigations into Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) and Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola) as a primary attack line against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, linking the government's inner circle to corruption and influence-peddling suspicions. The strategy aims to keep the cases in the spotlight throughout the race and revive anti-PT sentiment among voters, with campaign coordinator Senator Rogério Marinho arguing it is natural to raise the issue. The selection of Alfredo Gaspar as running mate — who, as rapporteur of the INSS CPMI, urged Lulinha's indictment — reinforces this tactic.

item.title: TRE questiona nome “Negona do Bolsonaro” usado por candidata do PL
item.description: The TRE-RJ has given Vanessa da Silva Oliveira, PL’s federal deputy candidate, three days to justify her use of the nickname 'Negona do Bolsonaro' on the electronic ballot, stating it raises doubts about her identity. The court cited TSE Resolution Article 25, which allows nicknames only if they do not create confusion, and requested an updated state judiciary certificate to check for any legal proceedings against her.

item.title: Governo avalia ampliar compra de milho para reduzir risco de desabastecimento em meio a El Niño
item.description: The Lula government is evaluating an increase in corn purchases from 50,000 to 80,000 tons annually to strengthen public stockpiles and mitigate desabastecimiento risks due to the expected strong impact of El Niño by the end of 2025, which could affect agricultural production and raise inflation in 2027. Conab states that existing resources in the Public Stock Formation policy are sufficient, avoiding the need for budget supplementation at this time. The measure aims to ensure continuity of the ProVB program, which supports small livestock farmers with animal feed, amid forecasts of prolonged drought in the North and Northeast regions.

item.title: Investigado por tráfico de influência, Lulinha visitou Planalto 18 vezes desde 2023
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, visited the Presidential Palace (Planalto) at least 18 times between June 2023 and January 2025, according to data obtained via the Freedom of Information Act. These visits have gained significance due to Federal Police investigations into alleged influence peddling and corruption involving Lulinha and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, with whom he exchanged messages indicating participation in meetings with key government figures, including former chief of staff Marcola and Health Ministry executive secretary Berger. Lulinha’s defense claims the visits were strictly private, while the Presidency’s Secretariat of Communication (Secom) stated no public administration matters were discussed.

item.title: Zema promete acabar com bets no 1º ato se eleito
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) pledged that his first act as president, if elected, would be to abolish online betting via decree, citing the devastating impact of gambling addiction on Brazilian families, including debt, income loss, and psychological harm. He likened betting to a 'poison' and a 'cancer', prioritizing the immediate halt of offerings before discussing alternatives for companies in the sector.

item.title: Eleição para governador do Rio volta à pauta do STF nesta quarta
item.description: The STF resumed its judgment on whether the new governor of Rio de Janeiro should be chosen by direct or indirect election, following the cassation of Cláudio Castro's (PL) diploma. So far, the vote stands at 4 to 1 in favor of indirect election via the Alerj, with only Cristiano Zanin advocating for a direct popular vote. Ministers agree the process has become moot due to the proximity of the October general elections.

item.title: Artigo: 'Quem representa os evangélicos? A nova disputa eleitoral'
item.description: The official launch of Lula's re-election campaign on August 16, 2026, featured First Lady Janja and gospel singer Pastor Kleber Lucas, signaling an effort to engage evangelical voters. This strategy reflects the growing political significance of this diverse demographic, which varies by denomination, generation, socioeconomic status, and ideology. The inclusion of gospel elements does not indicate ideological conversion by the left but rather an attempt to bridge symbolic gaps with key segments of the evangelical electorate.

item.title: A volta dos que não foram: Paulo Melo, Zito e filhos de Picciani concorrem novamente no Rio
item.description: Veteran Rio de Janeiro politicians, including Paulo Melo and José Camilo Zito, are returning to the 2026 electoral race after previous failed candidacies and legal challenges. Zito, former mayor of Duque de Caxias, is running for state deputy under the PDT, facing potential disqualification due to administrative improbity charges. Paulo Melo, former president of the state legislature and convicted in the 'Operação Cadeia Velha', is running for state deputy under União Brasil, seeking to overturn a 12-year-and-10-month sentence for passive corruption and criminal organization.

item.title: Jingle gospel, carta e evento com evangélicos: como Lula busca se aproximar do segmento religioso
item.description: Lula's campaign has intensified efforts to engage evangelical voters, aiming to overcome Flávio Bolsonaro's lead of 53% in this segment according to a Quaest poll. While maintaining his stance against using churches as electoral platforms, the team is discussing a meeting with evangelical leaders in Rio de Janeiro to counter disinformation and highlight government policies benefiting this group, though internal divisions persist over whether such gestures appear authentic or opportunistic.

item.title: ACM Neto esconde nome do avô em campanha para atrair eleitor lulista na Bahia
item.description: ACM Neto, former mayor of Salvador and União Party candidate for re-election in Bahia, is avoiding the use of his full name (Antonio Carlos Magalhães Neto) in campaign materials, opting instead for 'Neto' to appeal to Lula-aligned voters. This strategy, led by marketer João Santana, aims to distance his image from the carlist legacy amid strong PT support in the state, where Lula won 72% of the vote in 2022. Despite a technical tie in polls with Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT), Neto is betting on neutral colors and slogans like '#TôcomNeto' to broaden his electoral base.

item.title: PT terá menor número de candidatos lançados desde 1994 nestas eleições
item.description: The PT will field 1,097 candidates in 2026, its lowest number since 1994 and 32.7% below the 2002 peak of 1,630. The party is prioritizing alliances with MDB, PSD, and other parties to strengthen Lula’s electoral bases, especially in state races, where it will run only 12 own candidates — the fewest since 1994. This strategy reflects a shift from running many candidates to supporting allies in competitive slates to maintain national influence.

item.title: Divergências sobre redes e ataques a rivais levam a trocas de marqueteiros de Caiado, Cury e Zema
item.description: Four of the six leading presidential candidates in polls replaced their campaign strategists before the start of electoral advertising, due to disagreements over social media tactics and attacks on rivals. Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Augusto Cury (Avante) updated their communication teams, while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) had already made two changes in his communications leadership. The shifts reflect efforts to calibrate campaign tone, particularly regarding criticism of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Mansão em Brasília era usada por lobista e Lulinha para reuniões
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, son of President Lula, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger used a house in Lago Sul, Brasília, for discreet meetings, according to a domestic worker’s testimony. The property, rented by Luchsinger, was visited at least twice a month, with Lulinha appearing alone on some occasions. Lulinha’s defense denies wrongdoing and states he is available to cooperate with justice.

item.title: Direita leva preço dos supermercados para a campanha eleitoral contra Lula
item.description: Brazil's right wing has intensified its 2026 electoral campaign by using rising supermarket prices as a central argument against the Lula government, with candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira emphasizing the impact on household purchasing power. The strategy echoes historical electoral tactics, such as the Real Plan in 1994 and the 2022 'Supermercado Bolsocaro' ad, demonstrating that cost of living remains a recurring and effective theme in Brazilian political mobilization.

item.title: Paes e Ruas divergem na solução para a retomada de territórios
item.description: Eduardo Paes (PSD) and Douglas Ruas (PL), candidates for governor of Rio de Janeiro, present plans to reclaim territories controlled by criminal factions, including joint actions with the Armed Forces and tracking criminal financing. Although their proposals resemble past efforts that failed in the long term, Paes emphasizes federal government partnership, while Ruas does not explicitly mention Lula’s support, who has been reluctant to authorize GLOs in Rio. The reclamation is mandated by the STF in the ADPF das Favelas, but the effectiveness of these strategies remains questionable due to the repetition of previously tested methods.

item.title: Tarcísio aumenta peso da segurança em plano de governo em meio a ofensiva de Haddad sobre indicadores
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas’ 2026 re-election government plan significantly increases focus on public security, raising mentions from 23 in 2022 to 54. It proposes the creation of an Intelligence and Innovation Center (CIN) with 24/7 monitoring, integration of civil and military police, firefighters, civil defense, and municipal guards, plus expansion of the Muralha Paulista network and use of artificial intelligence. Haddad challenges the transparency of Tarcísio’s crime statistics and seeks to sway voters by questioning the governor’s management, while Tarcísio counters with a more detailed security strategy.

item.title: Por que a 3ª via não consegue eleger presidentes no Brasil. Entenda
item.description: The difficulty of a third-way candidacy in Brazilian presidential elections is not merely due to lack of votes, but to a combination of historical, partisan, and strategic factors that prevent the consolidation of alternatives outside the Lula-Bolsonaro polarization. Experts note that centrist parties have historically prioritized joining governments and negotiating power rather than building independent national projects, and that third-way candidacies are often poorly planned, launched too late, and lacking solid foundations. Despite a segment of the electorate that identifies with neither left nor right, this group rarely translates into sustained support for a competitive third-way candidate.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro busca votos para Roscoe, mas esbarra em Cleitinho
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro campaigned in Minas Gerais to boost Flávio Roscoe’s gubernatorial bid, aiming to link him to the Bolsonaro movement. However, he faces resistance due to the popularity of Senator Cleitinho Azevedo, who, despite supporting Bolsonaro for president, leads in polls and has strong conservative backing. The PL is relying on Nikolas Ferreira and additional visits to strengthen Roscoe’s position, but shifting votes from Cleitinho remains a major challenge.

item.title: Pesquisas internas de Lula e de Flávio apontam direções opostas
item.description: Internal polls from Lula's and Flávio Bolsonaro's campaigns show opposing scenarios: Lula's tracking indicates a 5-7 point lead, while Flávio's shows a technical tie. Official polls, including BTG/Nexus and Quaest, confirm a tight race with Lula ahead, though his lead has been shrinking over the past month.

item.title: Brasil tem menos transparência em anúncios nas redes sociais que União Europeia e Reino Unido, aponta estudo
item.description: A study by NetLab/UFRJ and the Minderoo Centre at the University of Cambridge found that Brazil offers less transparency in social media advertising than the European Union and the United Kingdom. On platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and X (formerly Twitter), access to advertising data is rated as insufficient, unavailable, or insignificant, making it harder to monitor the influence of money in political discourse, particularly during an election year.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad gastaram ao menos R$ 2,2 milhões em anúncios no Instagram e no Facebook em 2026, mesmo antes do início da campanha
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad spent at least R$ 2.2 million on Instagram and Facebook ads in 2026 before the official campaign period began, according to a g1 survey using Meta’s Ad Library data. Although these expenditures are not considered irregular by the TRE-SP, they are not counted toward campaign spending caps and were estimated using the minimum value of each ad spend range reported by the platform.

item.title: De minuta de contrato a almoço reservado: entenda as suspeitas da PF envolvendo a relação entre Lulinha, Roberta e Marcola
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating suspicions of influence peddling involving businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, lobbyist; Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula; and Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), former chief of staff to the president. Roberta is suspected of having sent Marcola a draft contract for the sale of cannabidiol to the Ministry of Health without bidding, linked to a deal with the 'INSS Careca', already arrested for diverting INSS funds. WhatsApp messages also show Roberta and Lulinha discussing business at 'another level', with future plans in Switzerland, while Marcola reportedly opposed the involvement of Fernando Bittar, Lulinha’s former business partner.

item.title: ¡Llamad a la primera dama!
item.description: Brazilian women will be decisive in the October 2026 presidential elections, yet the absence of female presidential candidates from major parties reveals the disconnect between party politics and national reality, where women lead nearly all social struggles while facing a rising tide of femicides.

item.title: MPE se manifesta a favor da elegibilidade de Deltan Dallagnol em 2026
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry (MPE) has expressed support for Deltan Dallagnol’s eligibility in the 2026 elections, stating that his 2021 resignation from the Federal Public Ministry (MPF) does not constitute a barrier to candidacy. The opinion notes that 13 of the 16 disciplinary proceedings underway at the time were later archived, and the three terminated by his resignation had no potential to result in dismissal, undermining the basis of the TSE’s 2023 decision that annulled his candidacy. The MPE also considers Dallagnol’s departure from the MPF as politically motivated, reinforcing the legitimacy of his Senate bid in Paraná.
